_comment: Tier-2 for skfem adaptive_poisson#2, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. Claim: Basis.interpolate(u).grad has shape (dim, n_elements, n_qpoints), P1 gradients are constant per element so [:, :, 0] is the cheap per-element slice, and confusing the axis order gives silently-wrong jump terms -- 'ValueError operands could not be broadcast together if you try to dot the wrong-shape tensor with the facet normal'. Ran: MeshTri().refined(2) with ElementTriP1 (32 elements, 3 quadrature points), both slices contracted against a 2-vector normal, and a genuinely mismatched contraction. Printed: shape (2, 32, 3) confirmed, [:, :, 0] is (2, 32) and [:, 0, :] is (2, 3), and the P1 gradient variation inside an element is exactly 0.000e+00. 'SILENTLY WRONG' IS RIGHT BUT THE ValueError IS NOT: contracting the WRONG slice against the normal does not raise -- both slices carry the spatial dimension first, so the contraction is legal either way and returns a length-3 array (one per quadrature point) where a length-32 array (one per element) was meant. Nothing is broadcast wrongly; the wrong axis is simply contracted correctly. A broadcast ValueError only appears for an unrelated length mismatch, so try/except is not a guard -- asserting the result is n_elements long is. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 applies the documented fix at the pathology site -- the wrong slice per_qp_of_elem0 = g[:, 0, :] becomes the correct per-element slice g[:, :, 0]. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 10 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 'wrong_result_is_one_per_quadrature_point=True' (the contraction now returns 32 values, one per element) and 'wrong_slice_is_silently_wrong=True', so the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
